item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) is inviting applications for its Graduate Professional position in Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament in Geneva, Switzerland. The opportunity provides graduate students and eligible recent graduates with the chance to gain practical professional experience within a United Nations institution while contributing to research and programme activities focused on disarmament, international peace and security, gender, and youth engagement.

The Graduate Professional will work within UNIDIR’s Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme, supporting research, programme implementation, communication, coordination and administrative activities. The position is particularly suited to candidates interested in international relations, political science, international law, gender studies, disarmament, arms control, youth engagement and United Nations affairs.

The position is based in Geneva, is full-time, and is expected to begin in November 2026. The programme will run for six months, with the possibility of extension, and successful candidates will receive a USD 1,500 monthly stipend as a contribution towards living expenses in Geneva.

The application deadline is September 16, 2026, at midnight Geneva time.

UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme 2026 at a Glance

Detail Information
Organization United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR)
Position Graduate Professional
Programme Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament
Location Geneva, Switzerland
Starting date November 2026
Duration 6 months, with possibility of extension
Working rate 100% full-time
Stipend USD 1,500 per month
Application deadline September 16, 2026
Deadline time Midnight Geneva time
Experience required Professional work experience is not required
Language Fluency in English required
Application method Email application in PDF format
Application email unidir.recruitment@un.org
Subject line UNIDIR GPP – IntApp (Geneva)

About the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research

The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) is a voluntarily funded and autonomous institution within the United Nations system.

UNIDIR is one of the few policy research institutes in the world dedicated specifically to issues surrounding disarmament and international security. Based in Geneva, the institute conducts research, generates knowledge and facilitates dialogue and action on critical security challenges.

Its work helps the international community develop practical and innovative approaches to some of the most important issues affecting global peace and security.

The Graduate Professional opportunity therefore provides an opportunity to gain experience in an international policy environment while working alongside professionals engaged in research, multilateral affairs and disarmament-related programmes.

About the Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme

The Graduate Professional will work within UNIDIR’s Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme.

The programme focuses on generating policy-relevant knowledge and providing multilateral practitioners with practical tools that can help them incorporate a gender perspective into their work.

The programme also supports youth engagement across different areas of arms control and disarmament.

This makes the position particularly relevant for candidates who want to explore the connections between:

  • Gender and international security.
  • Youth and disarmament.
  • Arms control.
  • International peace and security.
  • Multilateral diplomacy.
  • United Nations policy.
  • International relations.
  • Political science.
  • International law.
  • Gender studies.
  • Conventional arms control.
  • Policy research and analysis.

What Will the Graduate Professional Do?

The selected Graduate Professional will support the work of the Integrated Approaches – Gender and Disarmament Programme under the supervision of the Head of Programme.

The responsibilities combine research, programme support, communications, coordination and administrative work.

1. Conduct Background Research

One of the central responsibilities will be conducting background research to support the programme’s activities.

This may involve gathering relevant information, reviewing existing materials, identifying useful evidence and helping programme staff prepare for research and policy activities.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable with research, information gathering and analytical work.

2. Support Programme Activities

The Graduate Professional will assist with planning and implementing programme activities.

These activities may include:

  • Meetings.
  • Workshops.
  • Conferences.
  • Field missions.
  • Other programme-related activities.

This responsibility provides practical exposure to how international programmes are organized and delivered.

3. Support Communication and Coordination

The position also involves day-to-day communication and coordination responsibilities.

The successful candidate may be required to help ensure that information is communicated effectively, stakeholders are coordinated and programme activities are properly organized.

Strong written and oral communication skills are therefore important.

4. Provide Administrative Support

The Graduate Professional will also contribute to administrative tasks required by programme staff.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, keeping track of deadlines and supporting organizational processes.

5. Perform Other Programme-Related Tasks

The Graduate Professional may be assigned other tasks as required by programme staff.

This means that adaptability and willingness to support different aspects of the programme will be important.

Key Skills and Interests Required

UNIDIR is looking for a candidate with a combination of research, communication, organizational and technical skills.

Research and Presentation Skills

Applicants should demonstrate strong research and presentation abilities.

The role requires the ability to gather information, understand complex issues and communicate findings effectively.

Strong Writing and Synthesis Skills

The Graduate Professional should be able to transform information into concise, high-quality written briefs.

This is particularly important in an international policy environment, where large amounts of information often need to be synthesized into clear and useful documents.

Organizational and Coordination Skills

The position requires the ability to manage multiple tasks and responsibilities.

Candidates should demonstrate that they can:

  • Prioritize competing responsibilities.
  • Organize work effectively.
  • Manage deadlines.
  • Coordinate activities.
  • Monitor progress.
  • Adjust plans when circumstances change.

Communication and Teamwork

Strong interpersonal and communication skills are required.

The successful candidate will work with colleagues and stakeholders from different national, cultural and professional backgrounds.

The ability to collaborate respectfully and communicate clearly is therefore essential.

Computer and Design Skills

Applicants should be proficient in standard software applications.

In particular, the position requires proficiency with:

  • Microsoft Word.
  • Microsoft Excel.
  • Microsoft PowerPoint.
  • Canva.
  • InDesign.

Experience with these tools can be especially valuable for preparing presentations, written materials, visual communications and programme documents.

Interest in International Peace and Security

Applicants should have a genuine interest in issues related to:

  • International peace and security.
  • Disarmament.
  • Gender.
  • Youth engagement.
  • Arms control.
  • United Nations work.

Candidates with an academic or professional interest in these areas may be particularly well suited to the opportunity.

UN Core Values and Required Competencies

The Graduate Professional is expected to demonstrate the core values of the United Nations.

These include:

  • Professionalism
  • Integrity
  • Respect for diversity

In addition, candidates are expected to demonstrate several key competencies.

Communication

The successful candidate should be able to identify the information needs of different audiences and adapt communication accordingly.

This includes:

  • Writing clearly and concisely.
  • Communicating effectively in speech and writing.
  • Sharing relevant information.
  • Keeping colleagues and stakeholders informed.
  • Understanding the needs of different audiences.

Teamwork

Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to work collaboratively with people from different national and cultural backgrounds.

The ability to contribute positively to a team while respecting different perspectives is important in a United Nations environment.

Planning and Organizing

The role requires effective time management and planning.

Candidates should be able to:

  • Use time efficiently.
  • Anticipate potential risks.
  • Plan for contingencies.
  • Monitor progress.
  • Adjust plans when necessary.
  • Ensure that assignments are completed effectively.

Creativity

UNIDIR also values creativity and innovative thinking.

Candidates should be willing to:

  • Suggest improvements.
  • Explore new approaches.
  • Offer alternative solutions.
  • Challenge conventional ways of approaching problems.
  • Identify new ways to improve programmes or services.

Client Orientation

The Graduate Professional should consider the people and stakeholders receiving services as clients and seek to understand their perspectives.

This requires an ability to listen, understand different viewpoints and incorporate those perspectives into one’s work.

Education Requirements

Applicants must satisfy one of the programme’s graduate-level education requirements.

Candidates must either:

  1. Be enrolled in a graduate school programme, meaning a second university degree or equivalent, or a higher-level programme; or
  2. Have already graduated with a qualifying second university degree and, if selected, commence the Graduate Professional Programme within one year of graduation.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to current graduate students and recent graduates.

Preferred Academic Backgrounds

Although the programme has a broader eligibility framework, UNIDIR states that preference will be given to applicants with postgraduate qualifications relevant to the programme’s thematic areas.

Relevant academic fields include:

  • International relations.
  • Political science.
  • International law.
  • Gender studies.
  • Disarmament-related fields.
  • Other relevant areas connected to gender, youth and disarmament.

Candidates from related disciplines may therefore benefit from clearly explaining how their academic background connects with the programme.

Is Previous Work Experience Required?

Professional work experience is not required to participate in the Graduate Professional Programme.

This is an important feature for students and recent graduates who may not yet have extensive professional experience.

However, demonstrated experience or interest in conventional arms control will be considered an asset.

Applicants should therefore use their application to demonstrate relevant academic research, volunteer activities, internships, projects, publications, coursework or other experiences that show genuine interest in disarmament and international security.

Other Eligibility Requirements

In addition to the educational requirements, applicants should meet several other expectations.

Candidates should:

  • Be computer literate.
  • Have experience or competence with standard software applications.
  • Be comfortable using Microsoft Office tools.
  • Have experience with graphic design tools such as Canva or InDesign.
  • Demonstrate a strong interest in the work of the United Nations.
  • Demonstrate personal commitment to the ideals of the UN Charter.
  • Be able to interact successfully with people from different cultural backgrounds and belief systems.
  • Demonstrate willingness to understand and tolerate differing opinions and perspectives.

English Language Requirement

Fluency in English, both written and spoken, is required.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in English and produce clear professional written materials.

Knowledge of at least one additional official United Nations language is considered an asset, although it is not stated as a mandatory requirement for the advertised position.

Stipend and Programme Duration

The Graduate Professional position offers a USD 1,500 monthly stipend as a contribution towards living expenses in Geneva.

The programme is:

  • Full-time at 100%.
  • Six months in duration.
  • Scheduled to begin in November 2026.
  • Potentially extendable beyond the initial six-month period.

Applicants should note that the stipend is described as a contribution to living expenses rather than as a full salary.

Important Stipend Rule

Successful candidates who already receive a stipend from another source, such as an educational institution, will have their stipend topped up to USD 1,500 per month.

This means that candidates receiving another qualifying stipend should not automatically assume they will receive an additional full USD 1,500 on top of their existing support.

Medical Insurance and Health Requirements

Graduate Professional applicants must provide proof of valid medical insurance coverage for the entire period of the programme.

Selected candidates must also provide a medical certificate of good health before beginning the programme.

The United Nations states that it does not accept responsibility for the medical insurance of the Graduate Professional or for costs arising from injury, illness or death that may occur during the programme.

Applicants should therefore take the medical insurance requirement seriously when considering the opportunity.

Learn More

Screening Questions

As part of the application process, candidates must provide brief responses to several screening questions.

Each response should be 250 characters or less.

Screening Question 1: Education

Applicants must explain how they meet the graduate programme requirement.

They should state:

  • Their latest or current educational qualification.
  • Type of degree.
  • Field of study.
  • Institution.
  • Country.
  • Starting date.
  • Expected completion date, where applicable.

Candidates should make sure this response clearly establishes that they are either currently enrolled in a graduate programme or meet the recent-graduate requirement.

Screening Question 2: English Fluency

Applicants must address their fluency in English, both written and oral.

The response should clearly communicate their ability to work professionally in English.

Screening Question 3: Software Skills

Applicants should explain their skills with standard software applications.

Particular attention should be given to:

  • Microsoft Word.
  • Microsoft Excel.
  • Microsoft PowerPoint.
  • Canva.
  • InDesign.

Candidates should be specific rather than simply stating that they are “computer literate.”

Screening Question 4: Organization and Coordination

Applicants should explain their ability to organize and coordinate multiple tasks.

Examples may include academic projects, research assignments, events, internships, volunteer activities, work responsibilities or other situations where they successfully managed competing priorities.

Screening Question 5: Written Outputs

Candidates should list relevant written outputs they have published and provide links where applicable.

Relevant outputs could include publications, research papers, policy briefs, articles or other substantial written work that demonstrates research and writing ability.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit the required application materials in accordance with UNIDIR’s instructions.

The application should include:

1. Cover Letter

Applicants must provide a cover letter explaining their suitability and interest in the Graduate Professional position.

A strong cover letter should connect the candidate’s:

  • Academic background.
  • Research interests.
  • Skills.
  • Relevant experience.
  • Interest in disarmament.
  • Interest in gender and youth engagement.
  • Interest in the United Nations.
  • Career goals.

to the responsibilities of the position.

2. Inspira Personal History Profile

Applicants must submit a PDF copy of an Inspira Personal History Profile (PHP).

UNIDIR directs applicants to the Inspira guide for instructions on preparing the profile.

3. Screening Question Responses

Applicants must provide brief responses to all five screening questions.

Each response must be no more than 250 characters.

Candidates should therefore be precise and avoid unnecessary background information.

How to Apply for the UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme

Applications must be submitted by email.

Applicants should prepare their required documents as PDF attachments and send them to:

unidir.recruitment@un.org

The application email should use the following subject line:

UNIDIR GPP – IntApp (Geneva)

The application materials should be submitted before the deadline.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the UNIDIR Graduate Professional position is:

September 16, 2026

The closing time is:

Midnight Geneva time

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly because the application requires multiple documents and specific screening responses.

Important Application Instruction: AI-Generated Applications

One of the most important instructions in the vacancy notice is that:

Incomplete applications and applications generated with artificial intelligence will not be processed.

Applicants should therefore carefully follow UNIDIR’s instructions and ensure that their application materials genuinely represent their own qualifications, experiences, writing and responses.

Candidates should also ensure that all required documents are included and properly formatted before submission.

What Makes This Opportunity Valuable?

The UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme can provide valuable exposure to the work of an international United Nations institution.

For a graduate student or recent graduate interested in international affairs, the opportunity can provide practical experience in areas such as:

  • Policy research.
  • Disarmament.
  • Arms control.
  • Gender and security.
  • Youth engagement.
  • International peace and security.
  • Programme implementation.
  • Multilateral work.
  • International organizations.
  • Research communication.
  • Conference and workshop coordination.

The combination of research and programme responsibilities can also allow the successful candidate to develop skills beyond academic study.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to graduate students and recent graduates who are interested in building careers in:

  • International organizations.
  • Diplomacy.
  • International relations.
  • Peace and security.
  • Disarmament.
  • Arms control.
  • Gender and security.
  • Youth policy.
  • International law.
  • Policy research.
  • Multilateral affairs.
  • United Nations programmes.

Candidates who have strong writing, research, communication and organizational skills may be particularly competitive.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should avoid treating the application as a generic graduate opportunity. The position has a clear thematic focus, and candidates should demonstrate genuine interest in the programme.

1. Connect Your Academic Background to the Programme

Explain how your degree and research interests relate to gender, youth, international security, disarmament, arms control or another relevant area.

2. Demonstrate Research Ability

Highlight research projects, dissertations, publications, policy papers or other work that demonstrates your ability to investigate and synthesize information.

3. Highlight Your Writing Skills

Because the position requires concise, high-quality written briefs, applicants should demonstrate their ability to communicate complex ideas clearly.

4. Demonstrate Organizational Skills

Use specific examples showing how you have managed several responsibilities, coordinated events or projects, or worked under deadlines.

5. Highlight Relevant Software Skills

Do not simply state that you know Microsoft Office.

Where appropriate, demonstrate your experience with Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Canva and InDesign.

6. Explain Your Interest in the United Nations

The position specifically requires a demonstrated interest in the work of the United Nations and commitment to the ideals of the UN Charter.

Applicants should make this connection clear.

7. Demonstrate Cross-Cultural Communication

Because UNIDIR operates in a highly international environment, applicants should highlight experiences working with people from different backgrounds, cultures or perspectives.

8. Keep Screening Responses Within the Character Limit

The 250-character limit is strict.

Candidates should write concise, information-rich responses and check the character count before submitting.

Location of the Programme

The Graduate Professional position is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

Geneva is an important international hub and hosts numerous international organizations and diplomatic institutions, including United Nations entities.

Working at UNIDIR therefore provides exposure to an international policy environment closely connected to global peace and security discussions.

Important Facts About the Opportunity

Before applying, candidates should remember the following:

  • The position is based in Geneva.
  • It is full-time at 100%.
  • The programme begins in November 2026.
  • The initial duration is six months.
  • An extension may be possible.
  • A USD 1,500 monthly stipend is offered as a contribution to living expenses.
  • Professional work experience is not required.
  • Graduate-level enrollment or a qualifying recent graduate status is required.
  • English fluency is mandatory.
  • Knowledge of another official UN language is an asset.
  • Medical insurance is required for the programme period.
  • A medical certificate of good health is required before commencement.
  • Five screening questions must be answered.
  • Each screening response must be 250 characters or less.
  • A cover letter is required.
  • An Inspira Personal History Profile in PDF format is required.
  • Applications must be submitted by email.
  • The application deadline is September 16, 2026.
  • The closing time is midnight Geneva time.
  • Incomplete applications will not be processed.
  • Applications generated with artificial intelligence will not be processed.
  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Visit HERE to learn more about the UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme 2026 in Geneva.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme?

It is a graduate-level professional opportunity within the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research, allowing eligible graduate students and recent graduates to support research and programme activities.

Where is the position based?

The position is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

When does the programme start?

The selected Graduate Professional is expected to start in November 2026.

How long is the programme?

The initial programme lasts six months, with the possibility of extension.

How much is the stipend?

The advertised stipend is USD 1,500 per month as a contribution towards living expenses in Geneva.

Do I need professional work experience?

No. Professional work experience is not required.

However, demonstrated experience or interest in conventional arms control is considered an asset.

What degree do I need?

Applicants must either be enrolled in a graduate school programme or have graduated with a qualifying second university degree and, if selected, commence the programme within one year of graduation.

Is English required?

Yes. Fluency in English, both oral and written, is required.

Knowledge of another official UN language is an asset.

Do I need to know Microsoft Office?

Yes. Applicants must be computer literate and demonstrate skills in standard software applications, including Microsoft Office tools. Canva and InDesign skills are also required.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is September 16, 2026, at midnight Geneva time.

How should I submit my application?

Applications should be sent as PDF email attachments to unidir.recruitment@un.org with the subject line “UNIDIR GPP – IntApp (Geneva).”

Can I submit an AI-generated application?

According to the vacancy notice, applications generated with artificial intelligence will not be processed. Applicants should therefore follow UNIDIR’s instructions carefully and submit authentic application materials.

Will everyone who applies be contacted?

No. UNIDIR states that because of the high volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Shortlisted candidates may also be asked to complete a further assessment.

Final Application Checklist

Before submitting your application, make sure you have:

  1. Confirmed that you meet the graduate-level education requirement.
  2. Confirmed your eligibility as a current graduate student or qualifying recent graduate.
  3. Prepared your cover letter.
  4. Completed your Inspira Personal History Profile.
  5. Converted the required documents to PDF format.
  6. Prepared responses to all five screening questions.
  7. Kept each screening response within the 250-character limit.
  8. Clearly demonstrated your English proficiency.
  9. Highlighted your Microsoft Office, Canva and InDesign skills.
  10. Demonstrated your research, writing and presentation abilities.
  11. Explained your organizational and coordination skills.
  12. Listed relevant published written outputs and links where applicable.
  13. Confirmed your interest in international peace and security, disarmament, gender, youth engagement and UN work.
  14. Ensured your application is complete.
  15. Used the correct email subject line: UNIDIR GPP – IntApp (Geneva).
  16. Sent the application to unidir.recruitment@un.org.
  17. Submitted the application before September 16, 2026, at midnight Geneva time.
  18. Reviewed UNIDIR’s instruction concerning applications generated with artificial intelligence.

Official Programme Information

Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy information and UNIDIR’s application instructions before submitting their materials.

View the official UNIDIR Graduate Professional vacancy

Candidates should also consult the official Inspira guidance when preparing their Personal History Profile.

Access the Inspira platform and guide

Conclusion

The UNIDIR Graduate Professional Programme 2026 in Geneva offers an important professional development opportunity for graduate students and qualifying recent graduates who want to build experience in international peace and security, disarmament, gender, youth engagement and United Nations affairs.

The position combines research with practical programme responsibilities, including background research, meetings, workshops, conferences, field missions, communication, coordination and administrative support. It is therefore particularly suitable for candidates who want to develop both analytical and practical skills in an international policy environment.

The opportunity does not require previous professional work experience, making it potentially accessible to qualified graduate students and recent graduates who can demonstrate strong academic preparation, research and writing skills, organizational ability, computer literacy and a genuine interest in the work of the United Nations.

The position is based in Geneva, Switzerland, begins in November 2026, lasts six months with a possibility of extension, and provides a USD 1,500 monthly stipend as a contribution to living expenses.

Applicants should pay close attention to the application requirements. A cover letter, Inspira Personal History Profile and concise responses to five screening questions are required. Each screening response must be no more than 250 characters. Applicants must also meet the English-language requirement and demonstrate proficiency with Microsoft Office, Canva and InDesign.

Most importantly, applications must be submitted before September 16, 2026, at midnight Geneva time. Candidates should prepare and submit their applications early, ensure that all required documents are complete, and carefully follow UNIDIR’s explicit instruction regarding applications generated with artificial intelligence.

item.content:encoded:
The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027 is now accepting applications from exceptional doctoral students whose research falls broadly within the humanities and social sciences and addresses important issues relevant to Canada and the wider world.

The prestigious doctoral scholarship provides substantial financial support, research and travel funding, mentorship, experiential learning opportunities, and access to a multidisciplinary community of Scholars, Fellows, Mentors, and alumni.

For the 2027 competition, applicants must first complete an eligibility verification process before they can access the full scholarship application. The deadline to request eligibility confirmation is October 2, 2026, while the final application deadline is November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship 2027
  • Category: Scholarship
  • Study level: PhD/Doctoral
  • Fields: Humanities and Social Sciences
  • Study location: Canada, with specific eligibility provisions for Canadian students studying abroad
  • Scholarship duration: Three years
  • Annual stipend: Up to $50,000
  • Research, networking and travel allowance: Up to $20,000 per year
  • Eligibility verification deadline: October 2, 2026
  • Reference deadline: October 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET
  • Complete application deadline: November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET
  • Application process: Two steps
  • Official organization: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation

About the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship

The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship is designed to support outstanding doctoral researchers whose work can contribute to important conversations and challenges affecting Canada and society.

The Foundation is not simply looking for students with excellent grades. Its selection approach considers the broader potential of applicants, including their intellectual curiosity, leadership potential, engagement with society, ability to communicate knowledge, and capacity to create meaningful impact beyond academia.

Successful Scholars become part of a multidisciplinary community where academic research is connected with public dialogue, mentorship, experiential learning, networking, and societal engagement.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for doctoral students who want their research to have an influence beyond academic publications and contribute to wider discussions about major social, environmental, political, cultural, and human challenges.

Scholarship Benefits

One of the major attractions of the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship is its combination of financial support and professional development.

1. Annual stipend of up to $50,000

Selected Scholars can receive up to $50,000 per year for three years to support tuition and living expenses associated with their doctoral studies.

Over the three-year scholarship period, this represents potential stipend support of up to $150,000.

The funding is intended to give doctoral researchers greater financial stability while they concentrate on their studies and research.

2. Research, networking and travel allowance

Scholars can also receive up to $20,000 per year for three years to support activities connected to their doctoral work.

This allowance can help support:

  • Research-related activities
  • Academic and professional travel
  • Networking
  • Participation in relevant events
  • Activities connected with Foundation programming
  • Other research-related opportunities

This additional funding can be particularly valuable for researchers whose projects require fieldwork, conferences, collaboration, or engagement beyond their home institution.

3. Mentorship and experiential learning

The scholarship goes beyond financial assistance by providing Scholars with opportunities to engage with Mentors and Fellows.

The Foundation’s programming can include:

  • Meetings
  • Masterclasses
  • Seminars
  • Conferences
  • Leadership development
  • Experiential learning
  • Interdisciplinary exchanges
  • Public policy discussions

These opportunities are designed to broaden Scholars’ perspectives and help them connect their academic research with practical societal challenges.

4. Multidisciplinary community

Successful applicants become part of a community involving Scholars, Fellows and Mentors working across different disciplines and sectors.

This community can provide opportunities to:

  • Exchange ideas across academic disciplines
  • Develop professional relationships
  • Learn from experienced researchers and leaders
  • Share research with broader audiences
  • Explore interdisciplinary approaches
  • Participate in conversations about major societal issues

5. Alumni network

Scholars also become part of the Foundation’s alumni network, which includes more than 500 alumni.

This creates a long-term professional and intellectual network that can continue beyond the three-year scholarship period.

Fields of Study and Research Themes

Applicants must be pursuing doctoral research broadly related to the humanities or social sciences.

However, being in one of these broad academic fields is not enough. The proposed PhD research must also address issues relevant to Canada’s future and align with at least one of the Foundation’s four foundational themes.

The four themes are:

1. Human Rights and Dignity

This theme focuses on issues surrounding human rights, dignity, equality, justice, inclusion, and the conditions necessary for individuals and communities to live with dignity.

Potential research areas may include questions related to:

  • Human rights
  • Social justice
  • Equality
  • Inclusion
  • Discrimination
  • Rights and freedoms
  • Vulnerable populations
  • Human dignity

2. Responsible Citizenship

This theme concerns citizenship, participation, democratic life, civic engagement, and the responsibilities individuals and institutions have within society.

Research connected to this theme may explore:

  • Democracy
  • Civic participation
  • Citizenship
  • Governance
  • Political engagement
  • Social responsibility
  • Community participation
  • Public institutions

3. Canada and the World

This theme examines Canada’s relationship with the international community and Canada’s role in global affairs.

Relevant research could address:

  • International relations
  • Globalization
  • Diplomacy
  • Migration
  • International development
  • Global governance
  • Canada’s international role
  • Cross-border social and political issues

4. People and Their Natural Environment

This theme explores relationships between people, society and the natural environment.

Potential research areas may include:

  • Environmental policy
  • Climate change
  • Sustainability
  • Environmental justice
  • Human-environment relationships
  • Natural resource governance
  • Ecological challenges
  • Sustainable development

Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal clearly demonstrates how their doctoral project connects with at least one of these four themes.

Who Can Apply for the 2027 Scholarship?

The Foundation has established specific citizenship and enrollment requirements.

Eligible applicants must fall into one of three categories:

  1. Canadian students enrolled at a Canadian university
  2. Canadian students enrolled at a university outside Canada
  3. International students enrolled at a Canadian university

This means international students can apply, but they must be enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university.

Importantly, international students who are residing outside Canada and enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible for this particular scholarship.

Therefore, applicants should carefully distinguish between citizenship and university enrollment when determining eligibility.

PhD Stage Requirements

The 2027 scholarship is specifically targeted at early-stage doctoral researchers.

At the time of application, candidates must be either:

  • In the first year of their PhD program, or
  • In the second year of their PhD program.

Applicants who are beyond the second year of their doctoral program should therefore carefully assess whether they meet the Foundation’s requirements before beginning the application.

There is no age limit for applying to the scholarship.

What Does the Foundation Look For?

Academic excellence is important, but the Foundation evaluates applicants more broadly.

The strongest candidates are expected to demonstrate several qualities.

Academic Excellence

Applicants should have an outstanding academic record and demonstrate strong intellectual ability.

Academic performance is assessed across the application, including:

  • Academic transcripts
  • Research proposal
  • Letters of recommendation
  • Overall application quality

The Foundation states that successful applicants stand out through the quality of their research and their academic excellence.

Intellectual Curiosity

The Foundation seeks doctoral researchers who demonstrate genuine curiosity and an ambition to explore important questions.

Your application should therefore demonstrate not only what you are researching, but also:

  • Why the question matters
  • What makes the research intellectually significant
  • What knowledge gap you are addressing
  • What new perspectives your work could contribute

Leadership Potential

Applicants should demonstrate potential to contribute positively beyond their immediate academic environment.

Leadership does not necessarily have to mean holding a formal leadership position. It can be demonstrated through:

  • Community initiatives
  • Research collaborations
  • Advocacy
  • Professional activities
  • Student leadership
  • Public engagement
  • Projects that have produced meaningful results

Commitment to Society

The Foundation places considerable emphasis on applicants who are interested in connecting research with society.

Strong applications should show how the applicant’s work could contribute to broader conversations or help address significant societal challenges.

Potential for Impact Beyond Academia

Applicants should think carefully about how their research can reach audiences outside universities.

This could involve:

  • Public policy
  • Communities
  • Civil society
  • Government
  • Professional organizations
  • Practitioners
  • Public education
  • Knowledge translation

The Foundation specifically emphasizes the importance of sharing knowledge and creating meaningful impact beyond academia.

Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing

The Foundation also values applicants who are willing to engage in dialogue, interdisciplinary collaboration, and knowledge exchange.

A strong candidate should therefore be able to demonstrate an openness to learning from people working in other disciplines and sectors.

Letters of Reference

Applicants must provide three letters of reference.

The three referees must include:

  1. One PhD supervisor
  2. One additional academic referee
  3. One referee from outside academia

The inclusion of a non-academic referee is particularly important because the Foundation is interested in applicants’ broader engagement and potential impact beyond academia.

Applicants should therefore select referees strategically rather than simply choosing individuals based on academic seniority.

A good referee should ideally be able to provide specific evidence of your:

  • Academic ability
  • Research potential
  • Leadership
  • Community or professional engagement
  • Communication skills
  • Commitment to societal impact
  • Potential for future contribution

How the 2027 Application Process Works

The 2027 competition introduces a two-step application process.

Step 1: Eligibility Verification

Applicants must first complete a short eligibility verification form.

This initial step allows the Foundation to confirm whether an applicant meets the scholarship’s eligibility requirements.

The eligibility verification request must be submitted by:

October 2, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day if they can avoid it. Reviewing the eligibility requirements in advance can help identify potential problems before submission.

Step 2: Full Scholarship Application

Only applicants whose eligibility has been confirmed will receive access to the full application form.

This means applicants cannot simply skip the eligibility verification stage and proceed directly to the full application.

The Foundation states that applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed.

Important 2027 Scholarship Deadlines

Applicants should keep track of all dates rather than focusing only on the final application deadline.

September 1, 2026

The 2027 application process opens, including the eligibility verification form.

October 2, 2026

Deadline to submit an eligibility confirmation request.

This is the first major deadline and should not be confused with the final application deadline.

Weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026

Mandatory information sessions.

Eligible applicants should pay attention to instructions from the Foundation regarding participation in these sessions. October 30, 2026 — 9:00 a.m. ET

Deadline for all three reference letters to be received.

Applicants should contact referees well in advance because the letters must be received by the deadline.

November 6, 2026 — 4:00 p.m. ET

Final deadline for submitting the complete scholarship application.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because the scholarship is highly selective, applicants should approach the application strategically.

1. Confirm Your Eligibility Early

Before investing significant time in the application, check:

  • Your citizenship status
  • Your university’s location
  • Your current PhD year
  • Your field of study
  • Your research topic
  • Your alignment with the four Foundation themes

This is especially important for international applicants because international students must be enrolled at a Canadian university.

2. Develop a Clear Research Narrative

Your research proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand:

  • The problem you are investigating
  • Why the problem matters
  • The research gap
  • Your research questions
  • Your approach
  • The expected contribution
  • The relevance of your work to Canada and society
  • How your research connects to the Foundation’s themes

Avoid presenting your project as merely an academic exercise. Explain why the research matters in the real world.

3. Clearly Connect Your Research to a Foundation Theme

Do not assume reviewers will automatically see the connection.

Explicitly explain how your research relates to one or more of:

  • Human Rights and Dignity
  • Responsible Citizenship
  • Canada and the World
  • People and their Natural Environment

A well-developed thematic connection can help demonstrate that your project fits the Foundation’s objectives.

4. Demonstrate Impact

Think beyond publications and academic conferences.

Explain how your research could potentially influence:

  • Public policy
  • Communities
  • Institutions
  • Professional practice
  • Public understanding
  • Social debates
  • Government decision-making

5. Choose Your Referees Carefully

Because three references are required and one must come from outside academia, applicants should begin approaching potential referees early.

Give referees sufficient information about:

  • Your research
  • The scholarship
  • Your achievements
  • Your goals
  • The Foundation’s themes
  • Why you believe you are a strong candidate

This makes it easier for referees to write detailed and relevant recommendations.

6. Demonstrate Engagement Beyond Academia

If you have participated in community projects, professional initiatives, policy discussions, advocacy, public communication, volunteering, or other activities related to your research, explain their relevance.

The Foundation is interested in researchers who can connect knowledge with society.

APPLY HERE

Why This Scholarship Is Different from a Conventional PhD Scholarship

Many doctoral scholarships primarily focus on financial support. The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship combines financial assistance with an extensive intellectual and professional development component.

The Foundation describes its scholarship as more than financial support, emphasizing mentorship, experiential learning, community engagement and knowledge sharing.

A Scholar therefore gains access to:

  • Substantial doctoral funding
  • Research and travel support
  • Mentorship
  • Leadership opportunities
  • Interdisciplinary discussions
  • Experiential learning
  • Professional networking
  • A multidisciplinary community
  • A long-term alumni network

For doctoral students interested in connecting academic research with real-world challenges, this broader model can be particularly valuable.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can international students apply?

Yes. International students are eligible if they are enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university.

International students residing outside Canada and enrolled at universities outside Canada are not eligible.

Can Canadian students studying outside Canada apply?

Yes. Canadian students enrolled at universities outside Canada can apply, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements.

Can students in their third year of a PhD apply?

No. For the 2027 competition, applicants must be in their first or second year of doctoral studies at the time of application.

Is there an age limit?

No. The Foundation states that there is no age limit for applicants.

Do applicants have to speak both English and French?

No. Applicants do not need to be fluent in both official languages. However, they must be able to communicate effectively in either English or French.

How much is the scholarship worth?

The scholarship provides up to $50,000 per year for three years, plus up to $20,000 per year for research, networking and travel.

Is the scholarship renewable?

The scholarship is structured as a three-year program.

Can Scholars receive other scholarships?

Yes, but the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship may be adjusted depending on funding received from other organizations, universities or institutions. Scholars must declare additional sources of income each year.

The Foundation states that, regardless of other funding, Scholars continue to receive the annual research allowance, while the annual stipend has a minimum level of $25,000.

Application Link

Applicants should begin by reviewing the official eligibility requirements and then completing the eligibility verification process.

Applicants with questions about the 2027 scholarship can contact the Foundation at scholarship2027@trudeaufoundation.ca.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027.

Conclusion

The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027 is a major opportunity for early-stage doctoral researchers in the humanities and social sciences who want to combine academic excellence with leadership, public engagement and meaningful societal impact.

The scholarship offers up to $50,000 annually for three years, an additional $20,000 per year for research, networking and travel, mentorship, experiential learning, interdisciplinary engagement and access to a community of more than 500 alumni.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The opportunity is open to Canadian students studying in Canada or abroad, as well as international students enrolled at Canadian universities. Applicants must also be in the first or second year of their PhD and their research must fall broadly within the humanities or social sciences while aligning with at least one of the Foundation’s four themes.

The first critical deadline is October 2, 2026, when applicants must submit their eligibility confirmation request. Those who pass the eligibility stage must then ensure their three references are received by October 30, 2026, and submit the complete application by November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET.

For prospective Scholars, the key to a competitive application is not simply demonstrating strong academic performance. Applicants should present a compelling research project, clearly articulate its relevance to Canada and society, demonstrate leadership and engagement, and show how their work can create impact beyond academia.

item.content:encoded:
Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027: Applications Open for Undergraduate Students Seeking Careers in Aerospace

Applications are officially open for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027, an internationally accessible program designed to help talented undergraduate women and gender-minority students launch and accelerate careers across the aerospace and aviation industries.

The 2027 application cycle opened on September 1, 2026, and applications must be submitted by October 4, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT). The official application portal describes the program as bringing together exceptional undergraduate students from around the world who are passionate about aerospace careers and want to become future leaders in the industry.

The program goes beyond traditional academic assessment. Applicants are evaluated as complete individuals, with attention given to their experiences, interests, aspirations, creativity, character, service, leadership potential and the contribution they could make to the wider aerospace community.

Official Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027 Application Information

Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027 at a Glance

Detail Information
Program Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027
Application opening September 1, 2026
Application deadline October 4, 2026
Deadline time 11:59 PM EDT
Target applicants Undergraduate women and gender-minority students
Age requirement At least 18 years old
Academic level Undergraduate
Required coursework At least one year toward an associate or bachelor’s degree
Academic major Any major is welcome
Career interest Aerospace industry
Nationality All nationalities may apply
U.S. citizenship Not required
Main experience Summer aerospace industry experience/internship
Mentorship One-on-one professional/executive mentorship
Professional development Included
Summit Brooke Owens professional development summit
Application platform Online
Recommendation One letter required
Personal statement Maximum 600 words
Mission Alignment Essay Maximum 300 words
Multimedia submission Under 250 MB and reviewable in no more than five minutes
Minimum GPA None stated

The application portal opened at 12:00 AM EDT on September 1, 2026 and closes at 11:59 PM EDT on October 4, 2026.

What Is the Brooke Owens Fellowship?

The Brooke Owens Fellowship was created to expand opportunities for undergraduate women and gender minorities who want to become leaders, innovators and contributors within aerospace.

The program is named in honor of Dawn Brooke Owens, an accomplished aerospace professional and pilot whose career included work connected with NASA’s Johnson Space Center, the XPRIZE Foundation, the Federal Aviation Administration’s Office of Commercial Space Transportation and the White House Office of Management and Budget. The initiative was founded by aerospace leaders who knew Brooke personally and wanted to create opportunities for a new generation of people who could bring similar talent, creativity, determination and commitment to service into the industry.

Today, the program focuses on providing career opportunities, mentorship, professional development, industry connections and a strong community for undergraduate women and gender-minority students interested in aerospace.

The organization is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit and has developed a substantial network of aerospace professionals, executives, mentors, host organizations and alumni.

Applications for the Class of 2027 Are Now Open

The Class of 2027 represents the 11th group of Brooke Owens Fellows, marking more than a decade since the program’s first fellowship class.

Applications opened on September 1 and will remain open until October 4, 2026. The latest official announcement confirms that the opportunity is available to women and gender-minority undergraduate students from all college majors who are interested in careers in aerospace and aviation.

This broad academic approach is important because aerospace is much larger than aerospace engineering alone.

Professionals working in the sector may come from backgrounds including:

  • Aerospace engineering
  • Mechanical engineering
  • Electrical engineering
  • Computer science
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Data science
  • Physics
  • Mathematics
  • Chemistry
  • Biology
  • Earth and environmental sciences
  • Business
  • Finance
  • Communications
  • Public relations
  • Art and design
  • Law
  • Public policy
  • International affairs
  • Government
  • Education
  • STEM outreach

The program’s FAQ explicitly states that applicants do not have to major in aerospace engineering. Students from engineering, science, business, communications, art, law, policy and other academic fields may apply if they are seriously interested in building a career in aerospace.

What Will Selected Brooke Owens Fellows Receive?

The Brooke Owens Fellowship combines industry exposure with mentorship, community and professional development.

For the Class of 2027, the official announcement states that successful Fellows will:

  • Participate in a summer internship with a host company.
  • Receive one-on-one mentorship from professionals aligned with their areas of interest.
  • Attend a professional development summit with the other Fellows in their class.

The Brooke Owens Fellowship also describes its broader program as providing access to paid internships and executive-level mentorship from senior aerospace figures, including executives, astronauts and industry leaders.

Summer Aerospace Industry Experience

A major element of the program is meaningful exposure to the aerospace industry.

The 2027 program announcement states that accepted Fellows will participate in a summer internship at a host company. This provides students with the opportunity to move from classroom learning into professional aerospace environments and develop practical experience in the sector.

Past Fellows have worked across areas such as:

  • Rocket propulsion
  • Satellite operations
  • Mission planning
  • Aerospace policy
  • STEM outreach
  • Engineering
  • Software
  • Space systems
  • Research
  • Communications
  • Other aerospace-related functions.

The fellowship is therefore relevant not only to students pursuing highly technical engineering careers but also to those interested in the business, policy, communications and social dimensions of aerospace.

One-on-One Professional Mentorship

Mentorship is another central feature of the Brooke Owens Fellowship.

Each Fellow is connected with experienced professionals who can provide guidance as the Fellow enters or develops within the aerospace sector.

The Fellowship’s current mentor structure pairs Fellows with hand-selected mentors, with relationships beginning before Fellows start their summer positions. Mentors support Fellows as they prepare for professional roles, navigate workplace challenges and make decisions about their longer-term careers. Many mentor relationships reportedly continue beyond the official summer program.

The program’s mentors have included senior aerospace professionals, astronauts, executives, engineers and other industry leaders.

For a university student preparing to enter a highly specialized sector, this kind of direct professional access can help with:

  • Career planning.
  • Understanding aerospace industry pathways.
  • Developing professional networks.
  • Navigating early-career decisions.
  • Preparing for internships and employment.
  • Learning directly from experienced aerospace leaders.
  • Building professional confidence.
  • Identifying future areas of specialization.

Brooke Owens Professional Development Summit

Selected Fellows also participate in the annual Brooke Owens Summit, which brings members of the fellowship class together for professional development.

The 2027 announcement confirms that successful Fellows will attend a professional development summit alongside their cohort.

The summit adds an important cohort component to the program. Rather than completing an internship independently, Fellows become part of a community of students pursuing careers across different parts of aerospace.

This can create valuable relationships that continue as participants move into graduate education, industry, government, entrepreneurship, research and other aerospace careers.

A Long-Term Aerospace Community

The Fellowship is designed to create more than a one-summer experience.

The official Class of 2027 application describes Fellows as joining a lasting community of:

  • Peers.
  • Mentors.
  • Aerospace professionals.
  • Industry leaders.

This community-based model can be particularly valuable in aerospace, where professional relationships, specialized knowledge and industry networks can play an important role in career development.

The goal stated by the program is not simply to help students obtain their first aerospace opportunity, but to help develop people who may eventually shape the future direction of the industry.

More Than 400 Fellows Have Joined the Program

The Brooke Owens Fellowship has grown significantly since its creation.

According to the program’s September 2026 announcement:

  • 418 undergraduate students have been accepted since the program began.
  • Fellows have come from nearly 40 U.S. states and territories.
  • Participants have represented 10 countries.
  • 124 companies have hosted Fellows for summer internships.
  • 105 mentors have helped support Fellows during their early careers.
  • Fellows have represented 147 schools.

These figures demonstrate that the fellowship has developed into an established pathway connecting undergraduate talent with the aerospace industry.

Detailed Eligibility Requirements

Before beginning an application, candidates should carefully confirm that they satisfy every current requirement.

The official Class of 2027 application page lists four principal eligibility conditions.

1. You Must Be an Undergraduate Student

Applicants must currently be undergraduate students.

They must have completed at least one year of coursework toward a bachelor’s or associate degree by the time they apply.

This means the program is aimed at students who have progressed beyond the very beginning of their undergraduate education.

2. You Must Be Interested in an Aerospace Career

Applicants must demonstrate genuine interest in pursuing a career in the aerospace industry.

Engineering and non-engineering career pathways are both accepted.

Candidates therefore should not assume that admission is restricted to:

  • Aerospace engineers.
  • Mechanical engineers.
  • Scientists.
  • Technical majors.

Students from other disciplines are encouraged to apply when they can demonstrate a credible connection between their interests and an aerospace career.

3. Applicants Must Identify as a Woman or Gender Minority

The Fellowship is specifically designed to increase opportunities for people underrepresented in aerospace because of gender.

The formal Class of 2027 eligibility criteria require applicants to identify as a woman or gender minority.

The organization’s FAQ specifically notes that this includes women and other gender minorities, including nonbinary and gender-nonconforming individuals.

4. Applicants Must Be at Least 18

Applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

Students From All Academic Majors Can Apply

One of the strongest features of the Brooke Owens Fellowship is that it recognizes the multidisciplinary nature of aerospace.

Students do not have to study aerospace engineering.

The official FAQ specifically welcomes applicants from academic backgrounds such as engineering, science, business, communications, art, law and policy, along with other disciplines.

The critical factor is whether the applicant has a genuine ambition to build a career and create an impact within aerospace.

Is There a Minimum GPA?

No minimum GPA is stated.

The Fellowship deliberately uses a broader approach to identifying talent.

The official application guidance notes that past Fellows have included students with very high GPAs as well as students whose academic records were considerably lower. The organization states that GPA represents only one imperfect way of assessing an applicant’s abilities and potential.

The FAQ similarly states that applications are reviewed holistically, with consideration given to factors including the applicant’s:

  • Personal statement.
  • Creative submission.
  • Recommendation.
  • Character.
  • Leadership.
  • Creativity.
  • Service.
  • Alignment with Fellowship values.

Students should therefore not automatically rule themselves out because they do not have a perfect academic record.

Documents You Need to Prepare

The application requires several supporting materials.

Applicants should start preparing these well before the October deadline because the process includes both conventional application documents and original creative work.

Updated Resume or CV

Applicants need their most recent resume or CV.

The Fellowship recommends making sure the document is accurate, polished and carefully proofread.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Academic activities.
  • Internships.
  • Paid employment.
  • Volunteer activities.
  • Independent projects.
  • Leadership positions.
  • Clubs.
  • Extracurricular activities.
  • Relevant community involvement.

Applicants should use the resume to show not merely academic performance but evidence that they could contribute effectively as a teammate and member of the aerospace community.

Academic Transcript

Applicants must submit their latest transcript.

Importantly, an unofficial transcript is acceptable, and the Fellowship actually encourages students to use unofficial versions when obtaining an official transcript would require paying a fee.

The transcript submitted must contain completed, graded coursework. The application guidance says it needs to include at least one full semester of completed grades, rather than only midterm results.

Applicants studying at a new institution who do not yet have an appropriate transcript there may use a transcript from their previous institution where applicable.

Note that the formal Class of 2027 eligibility section separately states that an applicant must have completed at least one year of coursework toward an associate or bachelor’s degree. Applicants should therefore ensure they satisfy the formal eligibility requirement, rather than interpreting the transcript-upload requirement as reducing it to one semester.

One Letter of Recommendation

Only one recommendation letter is required.

The recommender should be someone who genuinely knows the applicant and can provide meaningful evidence about their strengths, achievements and character.

Potential recommenders may include:

  • Teachers.
  • Professors.
  • Coaches.
  • Mentors.
  • Supervisors.
  • Club leaders.
  • Other appropriate professional or academic contacts.

A family member or personal friend should not be used as the recommender.

The letter should ideally provide evidence of the applicant’s character, creativity, consistency, service and impact in the communities in which they participate.

The official FAQ confirms that applicants need one recommendation and only one will be accepted.

Three Original Application Components

For 2027, applicants are asked to prepare three original works intended to help reviewers understand them beyond their transcript and resume.

These are:

  1. A Personal Statement of no more than 600 words.
  2. A Mission Alignment Essay of no more than 300 words.
  3. A Multimedia Essay in a format other than a conventional written essay.

Together, these submissions are intended to provide insight into three broad dimensions:

  • Professional and academic interests.
  • Personal character, values and passions.
  • Commitment to service, community and creating opportunities for others.

Personal Statement: Maximum 600 Words

The personal statement allows applicants to communicate who they are beyond their academic record.

Applicants are encouraged to discuss the passions, values, experiences, goals and personal qualities that have shaped them and their ambitions.

The objective is not simply to repeat a resume.

A strong personal statement should help reviewers understand:

  • What motivates you.
  • What experiences have shaped you.
  • What matters to you.
  • What kind of person you are.
  • Where you want your career to go.
  • What you would contribute to the Brooke Owens community.

The program specifically encourages applicants to be authentic, specific and reflective.

Mission Alignment Essay: Maximum 300 Words

The 2027 application also includes a Mission Alignment Essay, limited to 300 words.

This component asks candidates to reflect on the Brooke Owens Fellowship’s mission of expanding aerospace opportunities for women and gender minorities.

Applicants should explain why this mission matters to them and how they hope to contribute to it throughout their careers.

Potential themes include:

  • Creating more inclusive professional environments.
  • Mentoring future students.
  • Expanding access to aerospace opportunities.
  • Addressing structural barriers.
  • Using leadership positions to support others.
  • Helping future professionals enter and thrive in aerospace.

The Fellowship encourages applicants to connect their answers with their lived experiences and consider how they could use future leadership or influence to make aerospace more welcoming and equitable.

Multimedia Essay: Show Creativity Beyond a Written Application

The Multimedia Essay is deliberately different from a conventional university application essay.

Applicants must not submit another traditional written essay.

Instead, they should communicate their ideas through a creative digital format.

Past formats have included:

  • Short videos.
  • Original songs.
  • Spoken-word pieces.
  • Animations.
  • Graphic designs.
  • Podcasts.
  • Comic strips.
  • Other creative digital formats.

Multimedia Submission Requirements

The submission must:

  • Be fully digital.
  • Require no physical mailing.
  • Be accessible through commonly available software.
  • Not require passwords or obscure software.
  • Be reviewable or playable in five minutes or less.
  • Remain below 250 MB in file size.

2027 Multimedia Essay Prompts

Applicants can respond creatively to one of the prompts listed for the Class of 2027.

The themes focus on:

  1. A situation where the applicant had to be resourceful and work within constraints.
  2. An experience serving a community and the resulting impact.
  3. A project or activity in which the applicant became deeply engaged and demonstrated enthusiasm or creativity.
  4. A situation where the applicant challenged an established system, norm or assumption.
  5. How intentional decision-making has influenced the applicant’s actions and outcomes.

These prompts are designed to reveal qualities such as:

  • Resourcefulness.
  • Creativity.
  • Values.
  • Service.
  • Teamwork.
  • Enthusiasm.
  • Courage.
  • Independent thinking.
  • Leadership.
  • Self-awareness.
  • Intentionality.

Important File Submission Rules

Applicants should carefully test every file before submitting the application.

The Fellowship specifically warns that an application cannot be edited after submission.

Before submitting:

  • Test video links.
  • Confirm that file-sharing permissions work.
  • Make sure reviewers will not encounter access restrictions.
  • Check that all files open correctly.
  • Verify multimedia runtime.
  • Keep files below the required 250 MB limit.
  • Proofread written documents.
  • Confirm that the correct versions have been uploaded.

The application page also recommends including the relevant prompt directly with each original work so reviewers can easily identify the question being addressed.

One detail worth noting is that the current page explicitly identifies three original works, including the 300-word Mission Alignment Essay, while its later file-submission checklist lists the resume, transcript, recommendation letter, personal statement and multimedia essay without repeating the mission essay. Applicants should follow the live application portal carefully and prepare the Mission Alignment Essay because it is expressly listed as a required original work earlier on the official 2027 application page.

Are International Students Eligible?

Yes.

U.S. citizenship is not required.

The official FAQ states that students of all nationalities are welcome to apply, while the official application portal describes the fellowship as bringing together undergraduate students from around the world.

There is, however, an important practical qualification for international applicants.

Some aerospace opportunities may be subject to U.S. export-control or International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) restrictions. These requirements can limit eligibility for particular jobs or host-company roles based on citizenship or immigration status.

The Fellowship states that it works with Fellows individually to identify opportunities that fit their circumstances.

International students should therefore not interpret ITAR restrictions as a general ban on applying. They are eligible for the Fellowship itself, although the range of specific industry placements available to them may differ.

Virtual Information Sessions for the Class of 2027

The Fellowship is also hosting virtual information sessions for prospective applicants.

The published Class of 2027 sessions, with times given in EDT, are:

  • September 13, 2026 at 2:00 PM EDT
  • September 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT, featuring international students
  • September 28, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT

The session specifically featuring international students may be particularly useful for applicants with questions about citizenship requirements, aerospace placements and participation from outside the United States.

Ask a Brookie Application Support

Applicants who want advice from someone who has previously completed the fellowship process can use the program’s Ask a Brookie resource.

Past Fellows can provide guidance about matters such as:

  • Their fellowship experience.
  • How they approached application essays.
  • Internship preparation.
  • Joining the Fellowship community.
  • General application strategy.

For formal questions concerning eligibility, applicants are advised to use the Fellowship’s official eligibility information or contact its administration rather than relying solely on peer advice.

How Applicants Are Selected

The program emphasizes holistic assessment rather than relying on one numerical indicator.

According to its FAQ, applications are reviewed by aerospace professionals and Brooke Owens alumni.

The program considers the overall application, including personal and creative materials, recommendations and alignment with the Fellowship’s values. There is no published minimum GPA cutoff and no single factor automatically determines selection.

This makes it important for applicants to submit a coherent application where the different components reinforce one another.

For example:

  • Your resume shows what you have done.
  • Your transcript gives academic context.
  • Your recommendation provides an outside perspective.
  • Your personal statement shows who you are.
  • Your Mission Alignment Essay explains how your values connect with the program.
  • Your multimedia project demonstrates creativity, character and perspective.

What Makes a Strong Application?

While there is no guaranteed formula, applicants should pay particular attention to the qualities the Fellowship repeatedly emphasizes.

Be Authentic

Do not attempt to construct what you imagine a stereotypical aerospace candidate should look like.

The application is specifically designed to identify talent that may not always be recognized through conventional recruitment methods.

Demonstrate Service

Community involvement is an important theme throughout the application.

Show what you have actually done for other people, organizations or communities.

Demonstrate Aerospace Interest

You do not need to study aerospace engineering, but your application should make it credible that aerospace is genuinely part of your intended career direction.

Show Creativity

This matters particularly in the multimedia submission.

Use a format that strengthens your message rather than selecting something elaborate simply because it appears impressive.

Explain Your Values

The program wants to understand what motivates your decisions and how your values affect the way you work with others.

Proofread Everything

A creative application can still be weakened by avoidable mistakes, inaccessible links or unclear writing.

Start Early

The application includes several components requiring substantial reflection, plus a recommendation from another person. Waiting until the final day substantially increases the risk of an incomplete or technically flawed application.

Application Timeline

September 1, 2026

Applications officially opened at 12:00 AM EDT.

September 13, 2026

First Class of 2027 virtual information session at 2:00 PM EDT.

September 19, 2026

International-student-focused virtual information session at 12:00 PM EDT.

September 28, 2026

Final listed virtual information session at 10:00 PM EDT.

October 4, 2026

Application deadline at 11:59 PM EDT.

The Fellowship’s FAQ indicates that semifinalists are typically contacted within several weeks after applications close, with finalists subsequently selected through interviews and the complete class announced during the winter.

How to Apply for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027

Prospective applicants should:

  1. Confirm that they meet the Class of 2027 eligibility requirements.
  2. Review the entire official application guide.
  3. Create an account in the application portal.
  4. Prepare an updated resume or CV.
  5. Obtain an appropriate academic transcript.
  6. Select one recommender and provide sufficient time for the recommendation.
  7. Draft the Personal Statement within the 600-word limit.
  8. Prepare the Mission Alignment Essay within the 300-word limit.
  9. Select one multimedia prompt.
  10. Create an original non-prose multimedia submission.
  11. Confirm that the multimedia content is reviewable in five minutes or less.
  12. Keep the relevant digital file under 250 MB.
  13. Check links, permissions and file accessibility.
  14. Review the entire application carefully.
  15. Submit before October 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT.
  16. Do not wait until the final minutes because applications cannot be corrected after submission.

Apply for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027

Why Students Interested in Aerospace Should Consider Applying

The Brooke Owens Fellowship offers something difficult to reproduce through an ordinary internship application: a combination of industry experience, structured mentorship, professional development and access to a continuing aerospace community.

The program’s record now includes hundreds of Fellows, more than one hundred host organizations and more than one hundred mentors. Its alumni network extends across aerospace research, engineering, operations, policy, technology, entrepreneurship and other areas.

For students who are serious about aerospace but have not traditionally seen themselves represented in the industry, the program is designed to create both access and a support structure for long-term career development.

Conclusion

Applications for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027 provide undergraduate women and gender-minority students with an opportunity to build professional experience, receive mentorship from experienced aerospace professionals, participate in professional development and join an established community of emerging aerospace leaders.

The program is intentionally multidisciplinary. Applicants do not need to major in aerospace engineering, there is no published minimum GPA, and U.S. citizenship is not required. What matters is that applicants meet the undergraduate and age requirements, identify within the gender groups the program serves, and demonstrate genuine interest in pursuing an aerospace career.

The application is more extensive than a conventional internship form. Candidates need to prepare a resume or CV, academic transcript, one recommendation letter, a Personal Statement, a Mission Alignment Essay and a creative Multimedia Essay. Applicants should therefore start preparing their materials early.

Applications close October 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT.
